name: PT J Resources Asia Pasifik Tbk

frontmatter.title: J Resources Asia Pasifik — one mine, a large cash pile and a price that already assumes more
frontmatter.summary: An update with a lower target than the initiation and a move to HOLD. The 30 September pack shortened the DCF stub, raised debt and left two June-keyed bridge lines stale; corrected, and with the Bakan M&I outside the reserve marked on the same basis as Seruyung, fundamental value is Rp256 and the konglo lens sets the target at Rp368, still below the Rp424 price.
thesis: The Doup disposal reset the company from a two-mine, high-leverage producer to a single-mine, net-cash one, but the market still capitalises the smaller asset base at a large premium to our fundamental value.

Bakan's stated P&P reserve supports under three years at the mine's actual run-rate; the company's five-year sufficiency claim is not reserve-backed, and the conversion that would extend the mine sits in the bull case, so the base carries no terminal value.

The Bakan M&I outside the reserve is now marked on the same conversion ratio and per-ounce bracket as Seruyung; that correction, not a change in the mine plan, is why the target is above the first pass on the September pack.
The interim dividend was a quarter of H1 profit including the Doup gain; the forward payout is the same policy on recurring profit, so the trailing yield is a capital return, not a run-rate.

The controlling shareholder holds almost all the shares and the public float is thin; the two free-float compliance steps and the MSCI Standalone consultation keep the concentration premium from closing quickly.
At the current price the shares still discount a gold price above the deck's through-cycle mark, so the risk-reward is balanced rather than attractive; the rating is HOLD.

catalysts.event: FY2026 annual report: Bakan reserve restatement, first full year without Doup, realised gold price
Free-float first step: the public float must reach the first tier, by controller sell-down or new shares
MSCI decision on the Standalone proposal for Indonesia; index increases remain frozen until then
Free-float final step: the public float must reach the full minimum
Archived September-quarter LK: confirms the cash-and-investments split behind the equity bridge
Any further step-up in the gold royalty schedule after the postponement announced in 2026

blocks.text: An update with a changed rating, not a changed mine. The data pack rolled from the 30 June to the 30 September 2026 balance sheet [S0], which shortened the FY2026 stub in our life-of-inventory DCF from the second half to the fourth quarter and refreshed net cash. Two bridge lines were still keyed to June — the gross interim dividend, already inside September cash after its 29 September payment, and the working-capital fraction, which must match the shorter stub — and both understated value. Corrected, and with the Bakan M&I outside the reserve marked on the same basis as Seruyung, the arithmetic settles at a twelve-month target of Rp368; the operating forecast, deck path and reserve base are unchanged. The rating is HOLD, against a price of Rp424 and a total return of -9.96 per cent including the forward dividend of Rp14 [S0][S2][S4][S5].

The call rests on the shape after the Doup sale: one producing mine, Bakan, a written-down Malaysian remnant, and a balance sheet that moved from debt to net cash when the proceeds landed [S2][S4]. The life-of-inventory DCF carries no terminal value because the ore body depletes and there is no second asset; on the stated reserve it values the shares at Rp243 [S2][S3]. The ounces outside that reserve — Bakan M&I, Lanut and Seruyung — are added at sourced marks with the closure provision deducted, and Penjom is carried at the company's own post-impairment recoverable amount rather than at its probable reserve [S2][S4].

The price is 1.76 times today's fundamental value of Rp243, and Rp424 against the twelve-month fundamental of Rp256, so the concentration lens sets the target at Rp368 [S2]. At that price the shares still discount a gold price above the deck's through-cycle mark. The call changes on a Bakan reserve conversion that extends the mine, or gold holding above the deck mark; it breaks on a reserve downgrade or a large related-party use of the cash [S2][S3].

J Resources Asia Pasifik is an Indonesian gold producer listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Its producing asset after the Doup disposal is the Bakan mine, held through PT J Resources Bolaang Mongondow, which delivered the great majority of group output in FY2025; the balance came from Penjom in Malaysia, an operation that has been mined down to its last proven block [S2][S4]. Seruyung and North Lanut are in post-mining care and maintenance, so the revenue base is effectively one mine with one plant and one permitting envelope [S2].

The company reports in US dollars, sells doré and concentrate at quoted gold prices, and charges the royalty in general and administrative expenses rather than cost of sales [S2]. FY2025 gold production was 83.9 koz thousand ounces (F1), of which Bakan produced 77.4 koz thousand ounces (F14) and Penjom 6.5 koz thousand ounces (F15) [S2]. Net sales were US$288.8m (F5) against cost of sales of US$118.6m (F7), with a royalty charge of US$41.4m (F9) inside the operating cost line [S2].

The asset base is the case. Bakan carries proven and probable reserves of 219 koz thousand ounces inside a resource of 707 koz thousand ounces (F11, F12) [S2]. The company states a multi-year reserve sufficiency at its disclosed capacity ([S2], company profile), but that claim cannot be reconciled with its own P&P: 219 koz koz covers only a handful of years, and Bakan produced 42.6 koz thousand ounces in H1-2026 (F44), a run-rate that exhausts the reserve in under three years. The base therefore mines the stated reserve and stops; the M&I outside the reserve — 36.0 koz measured plus 460 koz indicated less the reserve — is a bridge mark, and the conversion that would extend the mine is in the bull case [S2][S4]. The H1-2026 article puts Bakan's proved reserve at 52.0 koz thousand ounces (F45), consistent with that arithmetic. The other ounces are real but small — Lanut 157 koz thousand ounces of reserve, Seruyung 184 koz of resource, Penjom 384 koz of reserve of which 379 koz probable (F31-F34) — and are marked in the bridge: Lanut and Seruyung on the per-ounce bracket, Penjom at the company's own post-impairment recoverable amount rather than at its probable reserve [S2][S4].

The group changed materially. Doup, held through PT Arafura Surya Alam, was sold to an Astra subsidiary at an enterprise value of US$540.0m (F16), completing in February 2026 with a first-half gain of US$298.0m (F17) [S3][S4]. Penjom was written down by US$102.9m and carries US$16.5m after 4,734 oz ounces of proved reserve were mined (F18, F21, F28) [S4]. What remains is a single-mine, cash-rich producer, a different company from the leveraged one in the FY2025 accounts [S2][S4].

The controlling shareholder is the President Commissioner, who holds 92.5% of the shares, leaving 7.5% in public hands, as disclosed in the capital-stock note to the FY2025 accounts [S2]. Management is therefore the same party as control, and the board's independence rests on the commissioner designated as independent [S2].

Gold is a price-taker's business: nobody here sets the price, and the durable advantages are ore grade, cost position, permitting and the ability to replace mined ounces with new reserves. Indonesian producers sell at the London price less a refining and treatment discount that moves with concentrate quality and refinery tightness; PSAB realised US$3,308/oz in FY2025 against US$2,310/oz the year before, tracking the quoted price rather than any company-specific premium (F3, F4) [S2].

The regulatory framework is the most important non-price variable. Royalties step up with the reference price: PP 19/2025 raised the rate to 16.0% once gold clears the threshold in the schedule [S7]. The FY2025 charge implies a blended take below the new rate because the higher schedule applied for part of the year only (F9, F5) [S2][S7]. A further increase was announced and then postponed in 2026, so we model the current schedule rather than a rising one [S6]. Permits issue through the national mining regime, and keeping Bakan's plan approved is a live operating risk [S2].

Costs are driven by diesel, labour, reagents and stripping, with fuel priced off the deck's Brent path and the company's fuel intensity [S2]. Revenue is in dollars while much of the cost base and all of the dividend are in rupiah, so a weaker rupiah flatters margins [S2]. Bakan's unit cost, on our build from the LK, sits below the deck's through-cycle gold price, which keeps a sub-scale single-mine producer in cash [S2]. We claim no global cost-curve quartile, because no named third-party curve for Indonesian gold is in the registry, so the quartile stays unverified [S2]. There is no diversification, no smelting and a short reserve life, so the moat is weak: the mine is valuable while the ore lasts [S2].

Demand is macro rather than industrial, following real rates, the dollar, official buying and the local-currency jewellery price, so the shares move with the metal more than with company news [S2]. The sector deck carries a through-cycle path anchored on lower real rates, and that mark drives every revenue line [S0]. Supply responds slowly because a new mine takes years to permit, so a price above marginal cost persists — the window PSAB sells into, on top of a second cycle in diesel, the rupiah and the fiscal terms that the company does not control [S2].

The FY2025 accounts are the last clean year of the old company. Revenue was US$288.8m, cost of sales US$118.6m, EBIT US$100.9m and EBITDA US$145.8m, with D&A of US$44.9m and capex of US$30.9m [S2]. EBIT is restated to the company's own operating profit (F27) and D&A to the notes, which include cost-of-sales depreciation and mining-property amortisation the pack omits, so EBITDA is the filing-consistent figure [S2].

Revenue is a sold-ounce build, not a produced-ounce one. FY2025 revenue of US$288.8m at the realised US$3,308/oz implies sales above the 83.9 koz produced (F1, F3, F5), an inventory drawdown; the FY2026E volume input is the H1-2026 sales run-rate, so the forecast revenue is on sold ounces and the drawdown is not extrapolated [S2][S4].

The first half of 2026 is not comparable. Net sales rose to US$160.6m (F19) and attributable profit reached US$177.8m (F20), but the profit contains the US$298.0m disposal gain and the US$102.9m Penjom write-off (F17, F18), so operating profit is a small fraction [S4]. Equity was US$435.6m at June with unrestricted retained earnings of US$186.4m (F23, F24), the first positive unrestricted balance in recent history [S5].

Earnings quality deserves a flag. The disposal gain and the write-off are one-offs in the same half-year, so reported profit says little about recurring earning power [S4]. Working capital is distorted by the held-for-sale block — US$234.4m of assets and US$12.3m of associated liabilities (F29, F30) — which is why the pack's working capital jumps in FY2025; on a line-item build the operating balance was slightly negative, so the company was funded by suppliers. We model a low single-digit share of revenue and do not extrapolate the negative balance, which rests on related-party and tax payables that need not recur [S2].

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the story. The archived H1-2026 filing shows cash of US$17.1m and investments of US$195.3m at 30 June against total liabilities of US$201.3m and equity of US$435.6m, so the disposal repaid the facilities and left net cash (F37-F39, F23) [S4][S2]. The pack has since rolled to 30 September with a single liquidity line and higher debt, so net cash is narrower; we carry the June split and reconcile it to the September total in the bridge [S0][S4]. The Rp793.8bn interim was paid on 29 September, one day before the balance-sheet date, so it is already in September cash and not deducted again [S5]. Minorities are negligible; we flag the unexplained fall from the FY2025 minority as an open governance question [S2][S4].

Our forecast runs the single mine to depletion. Volume starts at 78.5 thousand ounces in FY2026E, in line with the first-half sales run-rate, and is capped by the stated reserve, which is consumed over FY2026E-FY2028E; the window beyond carries no production, hence a zero terminal value [S2]. Revenue follows volume times the deck's gold path and the company's realised discount, royalty is charged at the statutory rate, and cash cost is the FY2025 cost of sales less royalty, D&A and the inventory movement, escalated with the fuel path — a cash cost per ounce, not the accounting cost of sales [S2][S6]. EBITDA is US$176.0m in FY2026E and EBIT US$134.0m, with capex of US$28.9m and D&A of US$42.0m [S2]. Tax is charged at 33.0% of pre-tax profit, the cash rate the LK actually bears — current-tax charges of the operating subsidiaries over the last two years average that level, above the statutory rate because the non-deductible items have not disappeared. The FY2025 deferred-tax benefit is not extrapolated, and the statutory rate is used only for the debt shield [S2].

Revenue and EBITDA fall after FY2026E not because gold falls but because the plan mines fewer ounces each year — a depleting asset, hence no terminal value — and capex tracks the mine plan, close to D&A [S2].

The cost build is an ounces build, not a physical one, and that is checkable. Cash cost is the FY2025 cost of sales of US$118.6m less the royalty charge of US$41.4m, the restated D&A of US$44.9m and the inventory movement implied by sales exceeding production (F1, F3, F5, F7, F9), divided by the year's produced ounces to a cost per ounce, then escalated on the deck's Brent path for the fuel share [S2][S6]. PSAB discloses no strip ratio and no bank-cubic-metre measure, and the model carries none: the template's strip-ratio input is inert at one and the per-ounce unit cost does the work, so a bcm description would be coal-template boilerplate for a plan the engine does not run. The company does not split diesel, so the fuel share is a deck assumption, flagged as such [S0][S2]. Calibration reproduces FY2025 EBITDA once EBIT and D&A are restated to the filing; the residual is explained by the part-year royalty step-up and the inventory drawdown implied by sales exceeding production (F1, F3, F5) [S2][S7].

Capital allocation is the open question. The stated payout basis is a quarter of attributable profit, which is how the 29 September interim was described (F22), and we model that forward rather than extrapolating the disposal-funded distribution [S5]. The interim was the stated payout on H1 profit that included the US$298.0m Doup gain (F17), so the same policy on recurring profit is smaller: the forward dividend of Rp14 per share is a capacity yield of 3.3% on today's price, not the trailing figure in the data pack, which includes a capital return [S0][S5].

A depleting single mine is valued on the cash it produces before the ore runs out, so the primary method is a life-of-inventory DCF with no terminal value. Multiples are not anchors here: the trailing base contains loss years, a disposal gain and a write-off, and the peer set is priced on resource stories with different reserve lives [S2][S4]. We carry the DCF at full weight and disclose multiples as context only.

The cost of equity is 12.4% — a dollar risk-free rate of 4.9%, a mature equity risk premium of 4.2%, an Indonesian country premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 1.13 — and with pre-tax debt at 6.9% and a gross-debt weight of 14.4%, WACC is 11.4% [S0]. The pre-tax cost of debt in the WACC is the deck's USD risk-free rate plus the corporate spread, not the lower historical interest-expense rate on the P&L line. The engine levers the industry beta on gross debt over market capitalisation; on a net-cash definition the debt weight would be zero, beta would be 1.00 and WACC higher, because after-tax debt is cheaper than equity, so the gross-debt convention does not flatter the target [S0].

The DCF produces an enterprise value of US$243.9m, worth Rp243 a share on the September balance sheet and Rp256 twelve months out. The equity bridge takes the 30 September 2026 net-debt position, reconciles the June cash-and-investments split to the September total, subtracts the working-capital correction and the closure provision, and adds the marks for the ounces outside the Bakan reserve [S0][S2][S4][S5]. The valuation date is the last balance sheet and the horizon is twelve months from the price date, so the first forecast year carries only the fourth quarter of FY2026, and the per-share value uses the spot rate of Rp18,039/USD [S0].

The bridge marks every omitted asset on one basis. It reconciles the June liquidity split (cash US$17.1m plus investments US$195.3m) to the pack's September total — chiefly the Rp793.8bn interim paid on 29 September, one day before the balance-sheet date and largely offset by second-half operating cash flow, so it is not deducted twice [S0][S5]. The working-capital correction removes the FY2025 held-for-sale unwind the DCF stub credits (F29, F30) [S2]. The US$16.0m closure provision is deducted here rather than carried as debt, and net debt is total interest-bearing debt including the related-party loan, deducted once (F36) [S2]. Outside-reserve ounces are marked: Lanut at the sourced per-ounce bracket, Seruyung at the reserve-conversion ratio, Bakan M&I outside the reserve at the same ratio — 36.0 koz measured plus 460 koz indicated less the 219 koz reserve — and Penjom at post-impairment value (F31-F34, F21, F35, F46, F47) [S2][S4]. The US$195.3m investments are credited at face; a haircut sensitivity is carried at zero probability because the H1-2026 filing identifies the instrument categories but not counterparties or any affiliate [S4].

The konglo overlay then re-prices mechanically: a lower fundamental value against the price widens the premium ratio to 1.76 times, and the base regime keeps 0.40 of the log gap, so the target of Rp368 falls less than fundamental value. The Bakan M&I mark is a separate, sourced correction — the same treatment as Seruyung — not part of the period move [S0][S2][S4][S5].

The rating arithmetic needs stating, because the target now sits below the one that carried REDUCE at the last publication. At the Rp424 price the twelve-month total return is -9.96 per cent including the Rp14 forward dividend, and the HOLD band runs from a ten per cent decline to a ten per cent gain; the previous publication carried REDUCE on a slightly deeper negative return. Excluding the dividend the same target would rate REDUCE, and the dividend is what holds the name in HOLD. We are not softening the view: fundamental value and target both fell this round, and the HOLD is mechanical — the return is measured against today's price and credits the payout [S0][S5].

The reverse DCF states what the market believes. It solves for the benchmark gold price that equates the DCF to the market price, so US$8,074/oz is a gross deck-basis number, comparable with the US$4,300/oz through-cycle mark [S0]. The model's realised price is 4,103.9, the same benchmark less the sourced realisation, so the implied and through-cycle figures are on the same gross basis and the gap is not a realisation artefact. At spot, US$4,153/oz, the same plan is worth less than the Rp243 through-cycle DCF value: spot sits just under the US$4,300/oz marker and the sensitivity grid's price axis moves the value by less than a tenth per column, so the NAV at spot is close to the through-cycle number and nowhere near the Rp424 price. We anchor on the through-cycle mark because revenue is priced off a path, not a point, and the gap to the price is not a gold-price artefact: the reverse DCF needs US$8,074/oz to close it [S0]. The dividend-capacity anchor is Rp14 a share on Rp424, a forward yield of 3.3% — low, and not enough to carry the valuation on its own [S0][S5]. The disposal cash is already in the bridge at face value, so we add no separate distribution option; a buyback below fundamental value is a signpost, not base-case value [S0][S5].

Gold price moves the value more than any operating variable — the signature of a price-taker with a largely fixed cost base — and the discount rate bites harder than for a long-life asset because value sits in the near years [S2]. Neither argues for a wider method set: a multiple would restate the same gold price with another label [S2].

The concentration lens then sets the twelve-month number. PSAB is on the HSC list as of 22 October 2026 [S12]; one shareholder holds 92.5% of the shares and the public 7.5%. The IDX rule requires the float to reach 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and the full minimum by 31 March 2028 [S10], so there are two dated supply steps, not one; the first is 4.6 months from the report date, and wider from the registry asof of 27 October. Each step needs a controller sell-down or new shares, either of which raises the tradeable base while leaving control unchanged, and a controller has little reason to sell at a discount or dilute itself [S10]. MSCI opened a consultation on Standalone status on 15 October 2026, with a decision by 30 June 2027 and index increases frozen until further notice [S11]; that date is a risk to the premium, not an index-inclusion catalyst. We agree with the mechanism and disagree with anyone who reads the target as a statement that the shares are worth that much today [S2][S10][S11][S12].

The largest risk is geological. The base already mines only the stated reserve, so a reserve downgrade or a failure to convert resource ends the mine earlier than the plan; the conversion that would extend it is what the bull owns, not the base [S2]. The bear captures the downside: gold below the deck mark, volume a tenth lower, weaker realisation and a higher discount rate, giving Rp204 [S2][S4]. The bull mirrors the discount-rate shock, so the spread is not one-sided [S2].

Second, the disposal cash. A controller with 92.5% of the shares can direct it into related-party transactions; the interim dividend is a friendly use, a related-party acquisition would not be, and nothing sourced rules it out [S2][S5].

Third, regulation and tax. The royalty steps up with the gold price, and a further increase was postponed rather than cancelled [S6][S7]. Permitting and the post-mining liabilities at Seruyung and North Lanut are further claims the operating forecast does not fully capture [S2].

Fourth, market structure. With 7.5% public and a large controlling stake, the stock moves on flows, and the concentration that supports the premium makes the exit narrow if it compresses [S2]. The dated events are the two float steps — 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and the full minimum by 31 March 2028 [S10] — and the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027, with index increases frozen until further notice [S11]. Those change the premium rather than the mine, so the regime lens carries them rather than a fourth business scenario; thin traded value is why a liquidity check precedes any position [S2][S0].

Two layers sit behind the target and they must be read separately. The business scenarios above shock the mine: Rp204 in the bear, Rp259 in the base and Rp303 in the bull, on probabilities of 25%, 50% and 25%. The regime lens then shocks the premium the market pays over that value on its own probabilities — 25%, 50% and 25% — giving Rp287, Rp360 and Rp464, which average to the Rp368 target. The regime outcomes are an independent overlay on the same fundamental value, not a second operating forecast: they close 0.80, 0.40 and -0.05 of the log gap in the bear, base and bull, which is why a business-base value of Rp259 becomes a twelve-month price of Rp360 when the market keeps part of today's 1.76 times premium [S10][S11][S12].

The bull is not heroic, and importantly it does not add a sixth year: it runs the same five-year plan on four shocks only — gold above the deck mark, volume above plan, a better realisation and a lower discount rate — giving Rp303 [S2]. The resource conversion that would extend the mine past FY2030 is priced once, in the bridge mark for the Bakan M&I outside the reserve; the bull's extra volume is drawn from that same block inside the five-year window, a rounding double count disclosed rather than hidden, not a sixth year. The tails are close: a leveraged bet on one ore body, cushioned but not transformed by the balance sheet.

A reserve statement that adds mineable years, a decision to return the remaining cash, or a gold price holding above the deck mark without a cost response would move us up [S2][S6]. A reserve downgrade, a related-party use of cash, or a distribution cut signalling strain would move us down [S2][S5]. We also watch the realised discount, the quiet way a gold miner loses margin [S2].

Ownership is the defining governance fact. The President Commissioner holds 92.5% of the shares and the public 7.5%, which puts the company on the HSC list and out of the headline index [S2][S12]. Minorities cannot block a related-party transaction; independence rests on a single commissioner [S2]. The float must reach 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and the full minimum by 31 March 2028 [S10]; MSCI's Standalone consultation is a flow risk, not a support [S11].

The largest financial asset is US$195.3m of investments. The H1-2026 filing identifies currency-linked investments, mutual funds and restricted time deposits but no counterparty, custodian or related-party exposure [S4]. For a company this closely controlled that is the modal value-leak channel; we find no affiliate in the archived sources, classify it as an optics-class disclosure gap, credit face value and carry a haircut sensitivity in the bridge [S4].

The audit is clean and unqualified [S2]. Related-party loans and service arrangements are normal for an Indonesian group this size but are where value leaks in a controlled company [S2]. The minority interest falls to a rounding item at September and the change is unexplained (no price, counterparty or cash payment), so we treat it as an open ownership question and credit no buy-in [S2][S4]. The closure provision is on the balance sheet and deducted in the bridge [S2].

The dividend record is short: the 29 September interim is the only 2026 distribution in the archived sources, described as a quarter of H1 attributable profit (F22) [S5]. That profit included the Doup disposal gain, so the trailing dividend in the data pack is extraordinary and should not be capitalised; the forward payout is the same policy on recurring profit [S0][S5].

On ESG the material exposures are water and tailings, land rehabilitation after closure, and the social licence around artisanal mining near Bakan [S2]. The company discloses reclamation obligations but not emissions or water-intensity data, so environmental performance is unverified [S2]. Governance, not the environmental record, is the binding constraint on the multiple.

The FY2026 annual report will restate Bakan reserves and give the first full year without Doup [S2]. The September-quarter pack has one liquidity line; an archived LK would confirm the cash-and-investments split behind the bridge [S4]. The royalty schedule can move once more after the 2026 postponement [S6]. The float is on a dated path: 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and the full minimum by 31 March 2028 [S10], with the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 and index increases frozen until then [S11].

Between updates we monitor quarterly production and realised price against plan, the Bakan reserve statement, the cash and investments and any related-party use of them, and the float against the compliance calendar [S2][S4][S5].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: Gold mean-reverts below the deck's through-cycle mark, the Bakan reserve conversion stalls and the mine runs off the 219 koz reserve alone, so the plan ends around FY2029; Penjom closes after its proven block is exhausted and no new ore is found at Upper Tobayagan. Volume runs 10% below base, gold 20% lower, realisation a further 3% lower on a weaker refining market, and the discount rate 150bp higher for a single-asset, thin-float name.

bull.narrative: Gold holds above the deck's through-cycle mark and Bakan converts measured and indicated resource into reserves as it has every year for twelve years, so the same five-year plan runs 10% more ounces over the same window; Penjom's tailings retreatment stays economic at the higher price. Volume runs 10% above base, gold 20% higher, realisation 3% better and the discount rate 150bp lower for a name whose single-asset concentration is offset by a net-cash balance sheet in the up-cycle. The bull does not add a sixth year - the horizon stays at five years and production still ends at FY2030E - because resource conversion beyond that window is priced once in the bridge mark for the M&I outside the reserve, not again as DCF volume. The extra volume inside the window is drawn from that same M&I, so the bull double-counts roughly US$4m of the bridge mark, a rounding item against the shock, disclosed rather than hidden.

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Reserve-backed, not resource-backed, and capped at the stated reserve. Bakan has 219 koz proven and probable reserves (F12). The company's five-year sufficiency statement at 70-120 koz/yr (S2 p.18) cannot be reconciled with that P&P number on its own: 219/120 is 1.8 years and 219/70 is 3.1 years, while the mine plan actually conducted - Bakan production of 42.590 koz in H1-2026 (F44) - runs at about 85 koz/yr and exhausts the reserve in under three years. The base therefore mines the 219 koz and stops; the M&I outside the reserve is a bridge mark, not base volume, and the volume extension from conversion sits only in the bull narrative. FY2026E 78.5 koz is the sourced H1-2026 sales run-rate: H1 sales of US$160.63m (F19, S4) divided by the FY2026E deck price of US$4,288.84/oz and the 0.954 realisation gives 39.3 koz in the half, i.e. 78.5 koz annualised. FY2027E holds that rate and FY2028E 62.0 koz depletes the 219 koz reserve exactly; the engine then carries zero from FY2029E. There is no FY2031-33 tail in the base.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual, not on a forecast spike: the FY2025 average gold selling price was US$3,308/oz (F3, S2 p.45) against the metals deck's FY2025A gold average of US$3,466.09/oz, a ratio of 0.9544. The 4.6% discount is the refining and offtake wedge on Metalor sales (94% of 2025 revenue, S2 p.179) and is held flat across the forecast. It is NOT fitted to the FY2026E deck level of 4,493.75, which is a peak year relative to the FY2027E through-cycle marker of 4,300; fitting to the peak would carry a trough realised price into the long run.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic price cap applies to gold; all output is sold at market (S2 p.179).

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0: this is an ounces-based gold model, not a coal-style bcm stripping model, so cost_per_bcm carries the cash cost per ounce directly. PSAB does not disclose a strip ratio or ore tonnes in the annual report, and inventing one would be an unsourced driver.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Cash cost measured the house way (EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS): COGS less royalty less D&A. FY2025 COGS of US$118.568m (F7, S2 p.92) contains depreciation of US$22.527m and mining-property amortisation of US$17.225m (note 29, S2 p.179) plus an inventory movement of US$8.130m (stockpile, work-in-process and finished-goods lines, S2 p.179). The royalty of US$41.353m is charged in G&A (F9, note 30) and is modelled on its own line, so it is not in this input. Cash cost is therefore (118.568 - 39.752 - 8.130) = US$70.686m on 83.909 koz produced (F1) = US$842.4/oz. Held flat in nominal USD to FY2030E, per the house rule that costs stay at the last actual in real terms; no unsourced efficiency gain or further drift is assumed.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Diesel is the dominant mining consumable but PSAB does not split it out; the engine default of 0.3 is retained so the brent series can move the cost base without an unsourced split. The effect is immaterial because the oil deck is flat after FY2027E.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero by construction: the whole FY2025 cash cost per ounce (US$842.4, i.e. cost of sales less royalty, D&A and the inventory movement) sits in cost_per_bcm, and the royalty and SG&A are modelled on their own lines. Splitting the LK's single cash-cost line into mining and processing would be an invented allocation.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: PP 19/2025 sets 16% for primary gold when the HMA is at or above US$3,000/oz (F25, S7) and gold has been far above that since 2024; the May-2026 proposal for a further increase was postponed (S6). FY2025's effective take was 14.3% (royalty US$41.353m on sales US$288.751m, F9/F5) because the 10% rate under PP 26/2022 applied until April 2025 — a transition blend, not the forward rate. Using 16% is therefore a small step-up versus the last actual, disclosed in section 3.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Sales are gold and silver (S2 p.179); the silver credit is not separately disclosed and is inside the gold realisation, so carrying a separate line would double count it. Zero.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: No other revenue line is carried, so the margin is inert; kept at the engine default.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Total D&A from the LK notes, not the pack: COGS depreciation of US$22.527m plus COGS mining-property amortisation of US$17.225m (note 29, S2 p.179) plus G&A depreciation of US$4.816m and G&A amortisation of US$0.289m (note 30, S2 p.180) = US$44.858m (F42) on 83.909 koz produced = US$534.6/oz. The data pack's US$15.386m is only the non-COGS subset (the G&A lines plus the below-the-line mining amortisation), which is why it is restated from the filing. Held at the unit-of-production rate across the plan.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 additions were US$11.102m of property, plant and equipment, US$12.201m of mining properties and US$7.625m of exploration and evaluation (S2 p.94 cash flow) = US$30.927m on 83.909 koz = US$368.6/oz, which matches the pack's capex line. Held flat: the exploration share (US$91/oz) is genuinely discretionary, but after the Doup sale Bakan is the only asset and the company has kept drilling to replace reserves (132 holes in 2025, S2 p.53), so cutting it would be an unsourced uplift. No expansion capex is carried because no project remains.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero from FY2026E: the only development project, Doup, was sold to PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara and completed on 11 February 2026 for a US$540m enterprise value (F16, S3). Seruyung and North Lanut are in post-mining care and maintenance (S2 p.18/p.55), not development.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 pack figure (US$224.3m) is not operating working capital: current assets of US$332.007m include US$234.362m of Doup assets held for sale (F29) and current liabilities of US$182.191m include US$12.281m of liabilities directly associated with them (F30), so excluding the held-for-sale block operating working capital was about US$2.3m at 31 December 2025. After the disposal the 30 June 2026 balance sheet carries working capital of US$9.4m on about US$309m of LTM sales, i.e. 3.0% of revenue, which is carried flat. Prepaid taxes of US$21.9m (S2 p.90) are a period item and are not treated as operating. No stockpile release is modelled. The model still starts the FY2026E change in working capital from the contaminated FY2025 close, so the prorated difference is backed out in the valuation bridge.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The LK's cash tax rate, not the statutory rate. FY2025 current tax was US$23.997m on subsidiary pre-tax profit of US$70.085m (consolidated PBT US$65.364m less the parent's US$4.721m loss), a 34.2% rate; FY2024's current tax of US$15.205m on US$47.753m of subsidiary pre-tax profit was 31.8% (S2 p.92/p.187). The two-year average is 33.0%, which is used. The consolidated effective rate looked lower (19.0% in FY2025) only because of an US$11.598m deferred-tax benefit that is a timing item, not cash; the group's current-tax line has run well above the 22% statutory rate in both years because of non-deductible items and Malaysian tax at 24%. A forward 33% keeps that structural gap rather than assuming it disappears without a source.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: This 5.2% is the interest-expense line, not the WACC cost of debt: FY2025 interest and finance charges of US$16.600m (S2 p.92) on opening debt of US$320.770m is 5.2%, and debt has since fallen to US$105.03m at 30 September 2026 (S0), so the interest path is small. The WACC uses the macro deck's USD risk-free rate plus the corporate debt spread, 6.864% in the current run, which is the engine's kd_pre_tax; the two rates are for different lines and the report shows the engine rate.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: The yield applies to the cash line only. FY2025 interest income was US$0.064m on US$28.3m of opening cash, about 0.2%; the H1-2026 filing splits liquidity into cash of US$17.06m and investments of US$195.35m (F37/F38), so 2.5% is used on the small cash balance - a market USD deposit rate, above the FY2025 actual but below a bond yield. The US$195.35m investments are non-operating assets credited at face in the equity bridge; their return is embedded in that face value, and applying cash_yield to them would count the same asset twice.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: debt fell from US$235.8m at FY2025 to US$66.6m at 30 June 2026 and the company has US$211.7m of cash (S0 latest balance sheet); there is no announced drawdown and the Doup proceeds are being returned rather than reinvested (F22, S5). Financing does not enter FCFF, so this only sets the interest path.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. The two large non-operating items of 2026 — the US$298m Doup disposal gain (F17) and the US$102.92m Penjom write-off (F18) — are one-offs already reflected in the June balance sheet and excluded from the forward operating model.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero forward. Non-controlling interests were US$115.2m at 31 December 2025, almost all of it the 20% of JRBM (Bakan) not owned (S2 p.179), but the 30 June 2026 balance sheet shows NCI of only US$0.01m (S0), so the minority has been bought in and the remaining subsidiaries are wholly owned. The FY2025 history therefore carries a much larger minority share than the forecast — the attributable earnings step-up is a real, balance-sheet-evidenced change, not an assumption.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The 29 September 2026 interim dividend of Rp793.8bn (Rp30/share) was explicitly set at 25% of the US$177.9m H1 attributable profit (F22, S5), and that H1 profit includes the US$298m Doup disposal gain (F17). It is the only 2026 distribution in the archived sources; the Rp105/share mid-2026 figure carried in an earlier draft is not in S5 and is removed, and the data pack's trailing dividend is not extrapolated because it includes a capital return from the disposal proceeds (S0). Forward, 25% of recurring attributable profit is the stated policy anchor and is carried on every year; the balance sheet is net cash, so capacity exists for more, but a special return is a signpost, not base.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue or placement announced; the Doup proceeds funded the dividend instead (S5).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Inert: the primary method is a life-of-inventory DCF with no terminal value, because the mine depletes. Set to zero rather than the house inflation default so no residual growth can leak in.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 G&A was US$69.267m (S2 p.180), of which royalty was US$41.353m (F9) — royalty is modelled on its own line, so the SG&A ratio must exclude it: (69.267 - 41.353)/288.751 = 9.67%. Held flat. The FY2023-FY2025 pack default of 31.6% is meaningless because it includes the royalty and the loss years.

challenges.challenge: The base plan draws 78.5 + 78.5 + 62.0 = 219 koz over FY2026E-FY2028E and then zero, a three-year mine life, while the qc justification for horizon.reserves and section 1 both rely on the company statement of five years of reserve sufficiency at 70-120 koz/yr capacity (S2 p.18). 219 koz at that capacity is 1.8-3.1 years, so either the reserve figure or the plan is misread; nothing reconciles the two, and FY2029E/FY2030E carry zero volume inside a five-year horizon.
challenges.answer: Reconciled: Bakan P&P is 219 koz at 31 Dec 2025, not a reserve that supports the stated multi-year sufficiency; the base mines the stated reserve and stops, FY2029E-FY2030E carry zero volume, and the M&I outside the reserve is a bridge mark with conversion in the bull case. S1 now states the irreconcilable company claim and the depletion arithmetic, including H1-2026 Bakan production of 42.59 koz [S2][S4].

challenges.challenge: Bakan measured and indicated resource outside the 219 koz reserve is 488 koz (707-219, F11/F12) and is valued at zero, while Lanut 157 koz P&P and Seruyung 184 koz MII are marked at US$193/oz in the bridge. The same mark on Bakan M&I is US$94m, Rp64/share, on the same asset the DCF already operates.
challenges.answer: Marked Bakan M&I outside the reserve (496 M&I less 219 P&P = 277 koz, distinct from the 488 koz 707-219 total because inferred is excluded) at the same 44% conversion and US$193/oz used for Seruyung and Lanut. Bridge item US$23.6m at probability 1.0; the corrected bridge is why the target moved from the first-pass 318 to 367.80 and the rating to HOLD [S2][S4].

challenges.challenge: US$195.35m of investments (F38) is added to equity value at face but produces no return in the model: cash_yield 2.5% applies to the 17.06m cash line only, so ~US$4.9m a year of income on the largest single asset is absent from FCFF, about US$43m of PV or Rp29/share.
challenges.answer: FCFF excludes interest income by construction, so the US$195.35m investments are credited at face in the equity bridge rather than double-counted as a yielding asset. cash_yield applies only to the US$17.06m cash line; applying it to the investments would add an asset already in the bridge. Section 4 and assumptions.cash_yield.basis now state this explicitly [S4][S0].

challenges.challenge: The US$195.35m of investments to various positions (F38) is 31% of market cap and 59% of the fundamental equity value, credited at 100% with no instrument, counterparty, custodian or related-party disclosure. For a 92.5%-controlled issuer this is the modal value-leak channel and the governance section does not address it.
challenges.answer: S4 identifies the instrument categories (currency-linked investments, mutual funds, restricted time deposits) but no counterparty, custodian or affiliate. Added a governance paragraph, an optics-class structure flag, and a zero-probability haircut sensitivity in the bridge so the unknown is disclosed rather than modelled; no affiliate was found in the archived text [S4].

challenges.challenge: The float analysis stops at the 12.5% step by 2027-03-31 and calls the 30 June 2027 index review a route for index money in, but the konglo deck says the exchange requires 15% by 2028-03-31 and that MSCI opened a consultation on 2026-10-15 to move Indonesia to Standalone with a decision by 2027-06-30 and index increases frozen.
challenges.answer: Added S10 (two steps: 12.5% by 31 Mar 2027, 15% by 31 Mar 2028) and S11 (MSCI Standalone consultation opened 15 Oct 2026, decision by 30 Jun 2027, index increases frozen). Section 6 now carries both steps as supply risk and recasts 30 Jun 2027 as a flow risk, not an inclusion catalyst; S12 confirms the HSC list [S10][S11][S12].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 reports pre-tax debt at 6.9%, but fund record cost_of_debt says 5.2% is kept and that it matters little; the engine uses kd_pre_tax 6.872% and D/E 0.1689 to lever an unlevered beta of 1.0 to 1.13 even though the 30 September position is net cash of US$96.16m. The reader cannot reproduce the 11.4% WACC from the file.
challenges.answer: The 5.2% is the historical P&L interest-expense line; the WACC uses the deck USD risk-free rate plus corporate spread, kd_pre_tax 6.864%. Gross-debt D/E 0.169 is the engine convention; a net-cash D/E would set the debt weight to zero, beta to 1.00 and WACC higher, so the convention does not flatter value. Section 4 and cost_of_debt.basis now align with the engine [S0].

challenges.challenge: The target subtracts next-12m DPS of Rp14, i.e. 25% of recurring FY2026E profit, while the company has just paid Rp30/share (Rp793.8bn, F22) on H1 profit and, per the payout basis, Rp105/share in mid-2026; the demonstrated cash return is roughly twice the modelled dividend on a net-cash balance sheet with no growth capex. The Rp105 figure is also not in S5 (grep returns no hit).
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced Rp105/share. The only sourced distribution is the 29 Sep 2026 interim of Rp30/share, 25% of H1 profit including the Doup gain (F22/S5). Forward payout is set at 25% of recurring profit, and section 3 now states the net-cash capacity and why the trailing yield is a capital return [S5][S4].

challenges.challenge: The report says the move since the initiation is a period effect but never states the prior target or decomposes the change between the shorter stub, the bridge corrections and the lens; the queue records the model target moving 377 to 318 while the packet carries 358, so the claimed direction cannot be verified from the document.
challenges.answer: Reconciled the move line by line: v1 target 377.37, first pass 318, current 367.80. EV 323.72->243.90 (-79.82) on the September pack and shortened stub; net debt 49.54->87.97 (-38.43); bridge -105.50->+4.96 (+110.46, of which dividend -43.85->-11.22, working capital -108.30->-54.07, Bakan M&I +23.6, haircut 0); v0 249.05->242.86; premium 1.763->1.8. The move is data-driven, not re-anchored [S2][S4].

challenges.challenge: The registry date is 2026-10-27 and the deadline 2027-03-31, which is about 5.1 months, not the 4.6 months in section 4 and the packet; section 4 also calls the price 1.9x fundamental while its own twelve-month fundamental of 238 implies 1.78x (1.89x is against today 224.65).
challenges.answer: Months to the next deadline is now 4.6 from the report date, wider from the registry asof 27 Oct. The premium is stated as 1.8x today's fundamental v0 242.86 against the price, and the price against the 12-month fundamental 256.29, both bases named so the ratio can be reproduced [S0][S10].

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF says the price discounts US$8,410/oz against the US$4,300/oz through-cycle mark, but the model realised ASP is 4,104-4,289 (deck x 0.9544); a realised gold price is being compared with a gross deck mark, and the spot figure of 4,126 has the same problem.
challenges.answer: The reverse DCF solves the gross benchmark, not the realised ASP. Implied gross 8,409 vs deck 4,300; realised ASP 4,103.9 is the deck times 0.9544. Section 4 now states the gross-vs-realised basis explicitly so the implied price is not misread [S0].

challenges.challenge: The FY2025A calibration gap is -6.95% (EBITDA 135.64 modelled vs 145.77 actual) and the justification addresses only the D&A definition (gap under 0.5%); the revenue leg is production versus sold ounces, 288.75/3,308 = 87.3 koz sold against 83.909 produced, which is left unquantified and could recur in the FY+1 revenue build.
challenges.answer: FY2025 revenue 288.751 / ASP 3,308 = 87.3 koz sold against 83.909 koz produced, an inventory drawdown. FY2026E volume is the sales run-rate and revenue is built on sold ounces; calibration.ebitda and section 3 now state the sold-vs-produced basis [S2].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 describes a cost build of mined volume at the FY2025 stripping ratio and unit cost per bank cubic metre, but the model has no strip ratio (a.strip_ratio 1.0 placeholder) and cost_per_bcm 842.4 is USD/oz; PSAB discloses no strip ratio. The sentence is false about the model.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now describes the ounces-based cash-cost build the engine actually runs: FY2025 cost of sales less royalty, restated D&A and the inventory movement, per produced ounce, escalated on the Brent path for the fuel share. The strip-ratio and bank-cubic-metre claim is deleted and the inert template input is named as inert [S2][S6].

challenges.challenge: Expected return -9.958% sits 4bp inside the -10.0% REDUCE boundary, so HOLD is mechanical; the report prints -10.0% and never explains why a target 9 points BELOW the published REDUCE (Rp377) now carries HOLD.
challenges.answer: Section 4 prints the exact total return as -9.96 per cent via the placeholder and states the HOLD band runs from a ten per cent decline to a ten per cent gain. It says the previous publication carried REDUCE on a slightly deeper negative return and that crediting the forward DPS is what holds the name inside HOLD [S0][S5].

challenges.challenge: The commodity card requires NAV at spot; s4 only says the same plan is worth less at US$4,153/oz with no number, and the dividend-capacity anchor is vague (low-single-digit yield).
challenges.answer: Section 4 now sets the spot mark of US$4,153/oz against the through-cycle DCF of Rp243 and the reverse-DCF US$8,074/oz, and states the forward dividend anchor as Rp14 on Rp424, a 3.3 per cent yield, all through placeholders. The engine has no spot-NAV output line, so the spot value is given against the sensitivity grid rather than a typed rupiah number [S0].

challenges.challenge: VAL_KONGLO_REGIME requires business and regime scenarios shown separately; s5 gives business bear 204 / base 259 / bull 303 but not the regime lens outcomes (bear 287 / base 360 / bull 464 at 25/50/25) that produce the Rp368 target, so the two layers cannot be told apart in the scenarios section.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now shows the two layers separately: business scenarios 204/259/303 at 25/50/25 and the regime outcomes 287/360/464 on the deck probabilities, averaging to the Rp368 target, with the compression shares c = 0.80/0.40/-0.05 stated and the overlay labelled independent of the fundamental forecast [S10][S11][S12].

challenges.challenge: s3's closing paragraph still says 'the cost build is checkable: mined volume at the FY2025 stripping ratio, unit cost per bank cubic metre with the fuel share escalated', but a.strip_ratio 1.0 is a placeholder, PSAB discloses no strip ratio (the assumption basis says so), and cost_per_bcm 842.4 is USD/oz. Coal-template boilerplate describing a model that does not exist; identical to the 08:02 item, unchanged.
challenges.answer: The closing cost-build paragraph in section 3 is rewritten to the ounces build actually modelled: cost of sales less royalty, D&A and the inventory movement, divided by produced ounces and escalated on the Brent path. The stripping-ratio and bcm sentence is removed, not reworded, and the inert input is identified [S2][S6].

challenges.challenge: The commodity card's output contract is still not met: s4 says only that at spot US$4,153/oz 'the same plan is worth less' with no number, and the dividend-capacity anchor is not quantified. A reader cannot see the NAV at the spot mark or the forward yield that anchors the equity.
challenges.answer: Section 4 prints the spot mark and the through-cycle DCF and reverse-DCF values, and quantifies the dividend anchor at Rp14 on Rp424, a 3.3 per cent forward yield. Because the engine exposes no spot-NAV line, the spot value is stated against the sensitivity grid rather than as a fabricated rupiah figure [S0][S5].

challenges.challenge: VAL_KONGLO_REGIME requires business and regime scenarios shown separately. s5 gives business bear 204 / base 259 / bull 303 but not the regime outcomes that actually produce the target (bear 287 / base 360 / bull 464 at 25/50/25), so the two layers cannot be told apart in the section that sets the scenarios, and business-base 259 sits next to a target of 368 unexplained.
challenges.answer: Section 5 carries the regime layer beside the business scenarios: 287/360/464 on the deck probabilities, the compression shares 0.80/0.40/-0.05, the premium ratio 1.76 times kept in part, and the probability-weighted Rp368. The text says the regime is an independent overlay on the same fundamental value [S10][S11][S12].

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative says Bakan M&I conversion 'extend[s] the mine beyond the five-year reserve-sufficiency window and restor[es] the FY2031-33 tail (about 120 koz)', but params.horizon is 5 (FY2026E-FY2030E) and the model's volume is 78.5/78.5/62.0 koz then zero, so the DCF literally cannot carry a 2031-33 tail. The stated mechanism and the Rp303 bull are disconnected, and the volume x1.10 is applied inside the same 219 koz reserve the base already exhausts.
challenges.answer: The FY2031-33 claim is removed from the bull narrative in assumptions and from section 5. The bull is now stated as four shocks only - gold, volume, realisation and WACC - on the same five-year plan with no sixth year, and the small double count from drawing the extra volume out of the bridge-marked M&I is disclosed [S2].

challenges.challenge: The report prints expected return -10.0% beside HOLD, but -10.0% is the REDUCE boundary (fund record reduce_max_pct) and the actual figure is -9.958%: mechanically correct, unexplained, and confusing next to a target 9 points below the published REDUCE.
challenges.answer: The report prints -9.96 per cent via the placeholder rather than the rounded -10.0, and section 4 adds the line that the Rp14 forward DPS is what holds the name inside the HOLD band against the published REDUCE on a slightly deeper return [S0][S5].

challenges.challenge: Typo renders the realised price as 'US$US$3,308/oz' in the first paragraph of s3's sold-ounce discussion.
challenges.answer: The double currency prefix is fixed: F3 and F4 now render once as US$3,308/oz and US$2,310/oz. The same class of unit duplication was corrected across the other USD-million fact references and F22 was restated in IDR bn, so the render no longer prints USD mm or file-currency suffixes [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: Bakan 488 koz of M&I outside the 219 koz reserve (707-219) is valued at zero while Lanut and Seruyung are marked at US$193/oz; at the same mark it is ~US$94m or Rp64/share. The US$195.35m of investments also earns nothing in the FCFF.

missing_bear_case.note: The US$195.35m investments are 59% of fundamental equity value with no instrument, counterparty or related-party disclosure; the 15% final float step by 2028-03-31 and the MSCI EM-to-Standalone consultation are absent, and the report reads 30 June 2027 as index inflow.

assumption_realism.note: Volume 78.5+78.5+62.0 = 219 koz exhausts the reserve in three years against the five-year sufficiency at 70-120 koz/yr that the horizon justification itself cites; FY2029E and FY2030E then carry zero volume, so the five-year DCF is really a three-year one.

evidence_and_citations.note: The Rp105/share June distribution in the payout basis does not appear in S5 (grep: no hits); the 4.6 months to the 2027-03-31 deadline is inconsistent with a 2026-10-27 registry date (~5.1 months); the clean-opinion sentence carries a bare S2.

valuation_method_fit.note: Life-of-inventory DCF is right and the bridge reproduces exactly (243.90-87.97+195.35-18.64 = 332.62 = Rp226.8), but WACC uses kd 6.87% and D/E 0.169 to lever beta to 1.13 while fund record says 5.2% is kept and the group holds US$96.2m net cash.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is measured and the lens is not one heroic input, but the target move from the initiation is never quantified or decomposed, so the period-effect claim cannot be checked; three separate omissions (M&I, investment return, payout) all point the same way.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Gold path, 0.954 realisation and 16% royalty read the decks consistently, but the reverse DCF compares a realised price with the gross US$4,300 mark, and the konglo deck MSCI Standalone consultation is reversed in section 4.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack of understatements: no value for Bakan M&I, no return on US$195m investments, DPS Rp14 versus the Rp30 just paid and the Rp105 mid-2026 return, beta levered on gross debt while net cash, and a mine life two years short of the company plan.

flags.message: a.volume moves -100% from FY2026E to FY2030E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The base is the stated reserve and nothing else: Bakan has 219 koz proven and probable (F12) and the model draws exactly 78.5 + 78.5 + 62.0 = 219 koz over FY2026E-FY2028E, then zero. FY2026E 78.5 koz is the sourced H1-2026 sales run-rate: H1 sales of US$160.63m (F19, S4) divided by the FY2026E deck gold of US$4,288.84/oz and the 0.954 realisation gives 39.3 koz in the half, i.e. 78.5 koz annualised. The company's five-year sufficiency claim at 70-120 koz/yr (S2 p.18) is not reconcilable with 219 koz P&P (1.8-3.1 years) and the mine plan actually conducted - 42.590 koz at Bakan in H1-2026 (F44) - so the base follows the reserve, not the claim. The step down to 62.0 koz in FY2028E is reserve depletion, not a demand forecast; the M&I outside the reserve is a bridge mark and the volume extension from conversion sits in the bull narrative only. [S2][S4]
